description: Synthetic golden vectors for the existing pure engine health/system_health.py and the real registry. kind ENGINE = asserted against the current engine; kind PENDING = a future Home Assistant / Health v2 semantic, NOT asserted, never a PASS. No live data, no real HA history.

engine_vectors.title: every check healthy and current
ONLY the checks the ten HA sensors represent are supplied (all healthy): 10/10 is not overall clearance
engine_vectors.note: Every represented check is healthy, as in a 10/10 reading. The engine still reports UNKNOWN overall (subsystems with no evaluated check) and NOT READY (three required checks missing).

engine_vectors.title: telemetry never updated -> UNKNOWN, never HEALTHY
a required check is absent from the snapshot: readiness fails closed but the overall label stays HEALTHY (gap M-04)
ESPHome availability unknown (available=None) -> UNKNOWN INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
ESPHome never observed -> UNKNOWN
ESPHome unavailable (available=False) -> FAILED ESPHOME_UNAVAILABLE, blocks control
a real WARNING and an UNKNOWN at the same rank: the label is WARNING, UNKNOWN stays visible only through contributing subsystems and readiness
UNKNOWN from an INFORMATIONAL subsystem alone: overall UNKNOWN with rank 1 (rank not comparable with the label, gap M-07)
RTC stall flag true (isolated or sustained, the engine cannot tell): WARNING RTC_STALL_DETECTED, does not block control
the same stall flag after 400 s of continuous stall: identical result (the engine has no stall-duration input; split is design-only, see P01)
correction in progress for 5 s: WARNING RTC_CORRECTION_ACTIVE and blocks control
correction in progress for 179 s: still WARNING (boundary)
correction in progress for 180 s: FAILED RTC_CORRECTION_STUCK (boundary)
correction active but its start time is unknown: UNKNOWN, never 'just started'
one failed correction, baseline older than the 1800 s window: WARNING RTC_CORRECTION_FAILURES_RECENT, does not block
same failure with recovered=true: still WARNING, text says recovered
failed correction but the baseline is only 600 s old (< 1800 s window): UNKNOWN, not WARNING (engine window semantics, mismatch M-11)
no failures, absolute counter large (4000): HEALTHY, a historical counter is not a current fault
automatic clock sync OFF: the uncorrected-drift check is SUPPRESSED with no reason code; overall HEALTHY, ready (gap M-10: sync-off is invisible)
NTP not synced: WARNING RTC_NTP_UNSYNCED
RTC read 200 s old: DEGRADED RTC_READ_STALE; the check has no FAILED tier
RTC stall and correction busy together: both codes reported at rank 2
telemetry 59 s: HEALTHY (boundary)
telemetry 60 s: DEGRADED (boundary)
telemetry 70 s: DEGRADED and still ready
telemetry 179 s: DEGRADED (boundary)
telemetry 180 s: FAILED MODBUS_TELEMETRY_STALE, blocks control (boundary)
telemetry 200 s: FAILED, blocks control
configuration 179 s: HEALTHY (boundary)
configuration 180 s: DEGRADED (boundary)
configuration 599 s: DEGRADED (boundary)
configuration 600 s: FAILED MODBUS_CONFIG_STALE, blocks control (boundary)
telemetry timestamp 30 s in the FUTURE (clock skew): the engine reports HEALTHY with age -30 (gap M-05; ecco_core treats a future time as never fresh)
HA restart: every counter baseline lost and every transaction flag unknown -> those checks UNKNOWN, overall UNKNOWN, not ready
ESP reboot: the since-boot counter went backwards (2 < 5) -> UNKNOWN 'counter went backwards', never HEALTHY
counter value unavailable (None) with a baseline: UNKNOWN
counter restarted at 0 after a long uptime (baseline 4000, counter 0): UNKNOWN
25 h night (fall-back 25 Oct 2026): telemetry 60 s old across the repeated hour, UTC-aware -> DEGRADED, correct
same instants rendered as Europe/London local datetimes sharing one tzinfo (01:59:50 BST -> 01:00:50 GMT): wall-clock subtraction gives age -3540 s -> HEALTHY (HAZARD M-06)
fall-back, 'now' in London local and inputs in UTC (different tzinfo): correct, DEGRADED
23 h night (spring-forward 28 Mar 2027): telemetry 60 s old, UTC-aware -> DEGRADED, correct
same instants as same-tzinfo London local (00:59:50 GMT -> 02:00:50 BST): naive age 3660 s -> false FAILED and not ready (HAZARD M-06)
fall-back: RTC correction active for 180 s across the change, UTC-aware -> FAILED STUCK
same stuck correction as same-tzinfo London local (01:59:00 BST -> 01:02:00 GMT): negative duration -3420 s -> HEALTHY, the stuck correction is missed (HAZARD M-06)
fall-back: failed-correction counter 5 -> 6, baseline 2400 s old, UTC-aware -> WARNING
same failure as same-tzinfo London local (01:30 BST baseline, 01:10 GMT now): negative elapsed -> UNKNOWN, the failure is not reported (HAZARD M-06, fails quiet)

aggregation_vectors.title: STANDARD FAILED is capped to the WARNING band and reported as a definite WARNING
INFORMATIONAL FAILED is capped to DEGRADED
INFORMATIONAL WARNING is capped to DEGRADED
a CRITICAL subsystem with only UNKNOWN evidence makes the overall UNKNOWN
WARNING and UNKNOWN at the same rank: WARNING wins the label
only SUPPRESSED results: the subsystem and the overall read SUPPRESSED, not HEALTHY
a diagnostic-only subsystem is excluded from the overall; HEALTHY elsewhere stays HEALTHY
only a diagnostic-only subsystem: nothing contributes -> UNKNOWN, never a fabricated HEALTHY
no subsystem results at all: UNKNOWN

pending_vectors.title: RTC stall: isolated/transient versus sustained presentation
pending_vectors.requires: H4 + owner decision O-2 (separate approval; registry reason-code change)
pending_vectors.semantics: A single stall episode shorter than a configurable duration is shown as a noted, lower-prominence condition; a stall that persists beyond that duration, or recurs beyond a configurable rate, is shown at WARNING or higher. The raw RTC_STALL_DETECTED boolean, its episode history and the WARNING-eligible record are always preserved and visible. A stall alone can never reach FAILED. A stall never clears an RTC_CORRECTION_ACTIVE/STUCK, NTP or failed-correction finding. UNKNOWN inputs are never reclassified.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HV-C01 and HV-C02: identical WARNING for any stall duration.

pending_vectors.title: Automatic clock sync OFF as its own visible condition
pending_vectors.requires: H4 + owner decision (new reason code in registry/health_reason_codes.yaml)
pending_vectors.semantics: When automatic clock sync is OFF the RTC row carries a distinct reason (working name RTC_SYNC_DISABLED) with a duration, instead of rtc_drift_uncorrected being silently SUPPRESSED. It must remain visible after a reboot (the dongle setting persists OFF silently). It must not be 'fixed' by any HA write.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HV-C11: SUPPRESSED, no reason code, overall HEALTHY.

pending_vectors.title: Coverage-qualified rollup
pending_vectors.semantics: A future rollup cannot read HEALTHY while a required check, or any check the contract marks automatic, has no evaluated result. It reports UNKNOWN, or an explicit coverage object with complete=false, depending on the owner choice.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HV-B02: overall HEALTHY with a required check absent; HV-A02: UNKNOWN only because whole subsystems are empty.

pending_vectors.title: UNKNOWN stays visible beside a definite finding
pending_vectors.semantics: The rollup exposes unknown_subsystems[] and unknown_checks[] as separate attributes so a WARNING label never hides an UNKNOWN.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HV-B06: the label is WARNING; UNKNOWN is visible only through contributing_subsystems.

pending_vectors.title: Future or negative-age evidence is UNKNOWN
pending_vectors.requires: H1 follow-up in the engine (runtime change, separate scope) and H3
pending_vectors.semantics: An observation time later than 'now' beyond a small skew allowance is UNKNOWN with a distinct reason (working name FUTURE_TIMESTAMP), never HEALTHY, matching ecco_core.freshness.

pending_vectors.title: Evidence attributes on every health entity
pending_vectors.semantics: Every health row and the rollup expose evidence_age_s, last_good_at, observed_at, source entity ids and provenance kind (raw / normalised / derived) per the contract section 4.
pending_vectors.engine_today: CheckResult carries age_seconds only for freshness and transaction checks; SubsystemResult and OverallHealthResult carry none of the others.

pending_vectors.title: Two-tier freshness (60/180/600 s) in Home Assistant
pending_vectors.semantics: Telemetry, configuration and RTC-read freshness are evaluated from the change time of the dongle's last-update text, reproducing HV-D01..HV-D10 boundary for boundary.
pending_vectors.engine_today: Engine proves the boundaries (HV-D*). The HA communications row evaluates the online flags only.

pending_vectors.title: Communications: unknown/unavailable is UNKNOWN or FAILED, decided explicitly
pending_vectors.semantics: The HA communications row distinguishes 'device previously seen and now unavailable' (FAILED ESPHOME_UNAVAILABLE) from 'state unknown / never observed' (UNKNOWN INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), as the engine does in HV-B03..HV-B05.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HA template: any state other than 'on' for either online flag is FAILED with MODBUS_TELEMETRY_STALE / MODBUS_CONFIG_STALE.

pending_vectors.title: Restart-safe transaction durations
pending_vectors.semantics: After an HA restart or ESPHome reconnect with a transaction flag already on, the duration check is UNKNOWN (start time unknown), not an under-reported duration and not HEALTHY, until the start time is re-established.
pending_vectors.engine_today: HV-C06 and HV-E01 prove the engine behaviour. The HA rows derive duration from last_changed and under-report across a restart (documented limitation).

pending_vectors.title: Counter-reset parity between the engine and the HA RTC row
pending_vectors.semantics: One agreed rule for a since-boot counter that goes backwards or is first seen after unknown: either UNKNOWN until a fresh window (engine, HV-E02) or baseline-only with no state change (documented HA behaviour). The contract must name one.
pending_vectors.engine_today: Engine: UNKNOWN (HV-E02, HV-E04). HA RTC row per its documentation: baseline only, no failure counted. HA Jinja was not evaluated in this job.

pending_vectors.title: Machine-readable UNKNOWN subtype
pending_vectors.semantics: An UNKNOWN carries one of: NEVER_OBSERVED, UNAVAILABLE, BASELINE_PENDING, COUNTER_RESET, START_TIME_UNKNOWN, NOT_EVALUATED, THRESHOLD_UNRESOLVED, FUTURE_TIMESTAMP. Free text is not parsed.
pending_vectors.engine_today: The subtype exists only as free human_reason text (distinct per cause, checked by the golden suite).

pending_vectors.title: Clock-change safe evidence age in Home Assistant
pending_vectors.semantics: Every age is computed from epoch seconds or UTC-aware times so HV-F01..HV-F09 give the UTC-aware answers on the 25 h and 23 h nights.
pending_vectors.engine_today: Engine is correct for UTC-aware and mixed-timezone inputs and wrong for same-tzinfo local inputs (HV-F02, HV-F05, HV-F07, HV-F09).
